domain_context: Pure command-boundary admission of one mechanically constructed candidate authorization command from complete server-owned resolver outputs. This is before downstream authorization.
rule: For a representable CommandBoundaryContext evaluated normally, the boundary returns READY if and only if exactly one qualifying trusted authentication row and exactly one qualifying complete route-binding row match the request, and every candidate-command value has exact provenance from the inbound request or those same unique qualifying rows. Every other normally evaluated in-scope context returns DENY without a downstream call.
applies_when: one fully supplied CommandBoundaryContext uses complete authentication and route-binding resolver lists that preserve multiplicity
the three selected typed Rules and command-boundary Operation evaluate normally
actors: trusted application constructing the candidate command and resolver context
inputs: CommandBoundaryContext with inbound request, complete authentication-evidence list, complete route-binding list, and candidate command
the qualifying trusted authentication and complete route-binding rows and candidate-command values for this same context
outcomes: READY when the unique qualifying rows and exact same-row command provenance all hold
DENY without downstream call for every other normally evaluated in-scope context

examples.given: Exactly one trusted authentication row and one complete matching route row are present, and every candidate-command value has exact provenance from the inbound request or those unique rows.
examples.when: The command boundary evaluates the fully supplied context and the candidate values come from those same qualifying rows.
examples.why: The unique-row and same-row provenance conditions hold. This does not authorize the downstream operation.

examples.given: Two qualifying trusted authentication rows with nonempty session identities match the requested evidence reference, even if their visible values are equal.
examples.then: The command boundary returns DENY without a downstream call.
examples.why: List multiplicity must not collapse into one evidence row.

counterexamples.given: Candidate-command provenance does not match the unique resolver sources.
counterexamples.when: The provenance Rule is false while another Rule may be true.
counterexamples.then: An implementation returning READY contradicts this draft rule.
counterexamples.why: READY requires every selected Rule, including exact provenance.

counterexamples.given: One unique qualifying authentication row and one unique qualifying route row match, and all candidate-command values have provenance from those same rows.
counterexamples.then: The implementation contradicts this draft biconditional.
counterexamples.why: The positive READY branch is required, not merely fail-closed denial.

counterexamples.given: Two matching trusted authentication rows or two complete route-binding rows are present.
counterexamples.when: A set conversion collapses duplicate list entries before checking uniqueness.
counterexamples.then: A resulting READY decision contradicts the draft rule.
counterexamples.why: Exactly-one semantics use list multiplicity, even for identical rows.

counterexamples.given: One qualifying trusted authentication row has session S1; another matching trusted row has an empty session and is not qualifying.
counterexamples.when: The candidate command uses the empty session from the nonqualifying row while the unique qualifying row remains S1.
counterexamples.then: A READY decision contradicts this draft meaning.
counterexamples.why: Command provenance must use the same unique qualifying row, not a separate row satisfying a weaker existence check.

boundaries: This draft describes the command-boundary READY/DENY decision, not downstream authorization ALLOW/DENY.
No behavior is asserted for exceptions, nontermination, missing resolver outputs or contexts outside the selected typed contract.

The current typed candidate-command-provenance Rule can use a nonqualifying row; it does not preserve this intended same-unique-row meaning. This is a known counterexample, not merely unverified equivalence.
The eight Auth SFOL valuations and native witnesses do not prove all-context preservation.
No production authentication, authorization, security, runtime isolation, EVF pass or F5 guarantee is asserted.
claim_ceiling: Owner-reviewable draft of one command-boundary decision meaning only. Auth-local admission does not accept this DomainSpec BusinessMeaning; no v2 predecessor, v4 FormalClaim, neutral TDE set, provider observation, F5 satisfaction or runtime_guarantees_observed follows.
